name: Trincas
why_it_matters: Started as a Swiss tea-room (Flury & Trinca, 1939) at 17 Park Street; converted into a restaurant by Om Prakash Puri and Ellis Joshua in July 1959. Kolkata's longest-running live-music venue — Usha Uthup's career began on this floor. Still family-run by the Puris.
insider_tip: Two bands rotate nightly from around 7:30pm — book a table near the stage, not the bar side. Cover charge applies during peak music slots; ask before sitting.

name: Mocambo
why_it_matters: Opened 1956 by Shivji V. Kothari; menu shaped by Italian chef Antonio Prandhe (Chicken Sicilian, Cannelloni, Chateaubriand). Designed by German architect Messerschmidt — booth seating, etched glass and brass fittings essentially unchanged for seven decades.
insider_tip: Walk-ins queue out the door from 7:30pm onwards; lunch (12:30-3pm) is the easier window and same kitchen. Ask for a banquette in the inner room — it's the original 1956 layout.
signature_address: 25B, Park Street, Park Street Area, Kolkata 700016

name: Peter Cat
why_it_matters: Opened by Nitin Kothari in 1975 (sister restaurant to Mocambo). The Chelo Kebab — saffron rice, butter, poached egg, kebabs — was Kolkata's invention; Taste Atlas ranked Peter Cat 17th most legendary restaurant globally in 2023. Waitstaff still in Rajasthani turbans and red cummerbunds.
insider_tip: There's no reservation system after 7pm — give your name at the door, then wait at Music World on the same block. The Chelo is the only main course you should order; everything else is supporting cast.
signature_address: Stephen Court Building, 18A, Park Street, Park Street Area, Kolkata 700071

name: Flurys
why_it_matters: Opened 1927 by Swiss partners Joseph Flury and Quinto Cinzio Trinca as a Swiss confectionery and tea room. Sold to Jit Paul in 1965 and now part of Apeejay Surrendra Group; the original Park Street tearoom remains the flagship of a 60+ outlet chain across India.
insider_tip: Breakfast is the meal Flurys does best — eggs, sausages, baked beans served until 11am. Skip the pastries on busy weekend afternoons and come for the morning quiet.
signature_address: 18, Park Street, Park Street Area, Kolkata 700016

name: Olypub
why_it_matters: Started as Olympia Bar and Restaurant in 1947, rebranded as Oly Pub in 1981 by its Parsi owners. Famous for an inexpensive beef steak and a regulars' bar that pulled Uttam Kumar and Satyajit Ray in their day. One of the few Park Street holdouts that still serves both beef and pork.
insider_tip: Two floors — ground level is the working-day pub, first floor is the family/restaurant section. Order the steak well-done unless you know the kitchen; the cooking on the rare side is uneven.
signature_address: 21, Park Street, Park Street Area, Kolkata 700016
